I recently stayed at this hotel in Bodrum, Turkbuku, an area I’m very familiar with. The overall design of the hotel is quite eye-catching, and the rooms were spacious, nicely decorated, and appeared clean. However, I had a few issues during my stay. First, the bedding: there was only one twin blanket provided on a queen-sized bed, which was uncomfortable for two people. Additionally, the room lacked basic amenities such as a coffee machine, water, or a kettle with complimentary drinks—something I would expect for early mornings or late nights spent in the room. Breakfast was decent, nothing spectacular, but not bad either. The beach area was a nice touch, and I appreciated the hotel providing towels for the beach. The Turkish coffee was great, but I ordered an iced latte, and unfortunately, there were coffee kernels in it, and the espresso itself wasn’t to our taste. Lunch was also just average, not bad, but nothing special. We paid $260 for the night on a deal, only breakfast included, though the regular price is listed at $300. At this price point, I expected more in terms of services and amenities. Overall, while the design and some aspects of the stay were pleasant, I believe the hotel could improve on the little details that make a stay truly comfortable and worth the price.
